title: White House Says Countries Are Sneaking Goods Past Tariffs
summary:
Have you ever tried to sneak a cookie past your parents by hiding it in a napkin? Well, the White House says some countries are doing something similar with goods to avoid paying US taxes called tariffs.

On Thursday, August 13, 2026, the Trump White House released a report saying countries are routing their exports through third countries to avoid US tariffs. They estimate the US is losing $19 billion to $26 billion every year in tax revenue because of this trick.

The report points a finger at China. It says China responded to tariffs in 2018 by sending goods to other countries like Mexico and Malaysia for packaging and small assembly work. This practice is called "transshipping." It makes it look like US imports from China dropped, but China's factories kept growing.

Peter Navarro, the White House trade adviser, said China is "laundering" its exports through more than 40 countries. He called it "the great transshipment scam." The report says other countries, like India, could also do this.

To fight back, US Customs and Border Protection is testing artificial intelligence to spot fake origins. If an importer is caught lying about where goods come from, they can be charged tariffs going back about a year.

This all comes before a planned visit by Chinese Leader Xi Jinping in September. President Trump has spoken nicely about Xi, but the report shows tensions over trade are still high. The US still imports more than it exports, but the trade gap is smaller this year than last year.
why_it_matters: This matters because hidden trade tricks can change the prices of toys, electronics, and other goods your family buys.

background_read: The US charges tariffs to make imported goods cost more, hoping to protect American factories and local jobs.
China is one of the world's biggest manufacturing countries and makes many products sold around the world.
US Customs and Border Protection is the agency that checks goods entering the United States.
Article_Structure: WHO: The Trump White House and trade adviser Peter Navarro.
WHAT: A report says countries are routing exports through third countries to avoid US tariffs, losing $19 billion to $26 billion a year.
WHERE: The United States, with goods passing through Mexico, Malaysia, and more than 40 countries.
WHY: The US wants to stop tax cheating and ease trade tensions, especially before Chinese Leader Xi Jinping's visit.

perspectives.description: They want to stop countries from dodging tariffs and protect US tax revenue and jobs.
They may see the tariffs as unfair and use third countries to keep selling goods abroad.
They may worry that stricter checks and backdated tariff bills will make imported goods more expensive.
